# s3orchestrator Provider

Manages the identities, keypairs and grants a running s3-orchestrator authorizes requests against.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    s3orchestrator = {
      source  = "afreidah/s3-orchestrator"
      version = ">= 0.1"
    }
  }
}

# Every attribute falls back to an environment variable: S3O_ADMIN_ADDR,
# S3O_ACCESS_KEY_ID and S3O_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, the same three the admin CLI and
# the TUI read. A shell configured for one is configured for all of them, so the
# block can be left empty.
#
# Naming the address here instead pins the configuration to one deployment,
# which is worth doing for anything that must never reach production by
# accident. The keypair stays in the environment either way, because a literal
# secret in a .tf file is a secret in version control.
provider "s3orchestrator" {
  address = "http://localhost:9000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `access_key_id` (String) Access key requests are signed with. Its user needs the `admin-provision` permission on the orchestrator. Falls back to `S3O_ACCESS_KEY_ID`.
- `address` (String) Base address of the admin API, for example `https://s3.example.com`. A bare `host:port` is reached over HTTP. Falls back to `S3O_ADMIN_ADDR`.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive) Secret half of the signing keypair. Falls back to `S3O_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
